title: When the Data Are Out: Measuring Behavioral Changes Following a Data Breach
eligible_reason: Not a staggered adoption design, and the data are a de-identified simulated sample. The Ashley Madison data breach is a single common date for all users. 'Temporal causal inference' compares join-week cohorts at the same membership age (earlier joiners observed post-breach vs later joiners pre-breach), and temporal causal forests estimate heterogeneity. The only DiD regressions are in a simulation study comparing DiD with local linear causal forests on simulated data unrelated to the breach (appendix).
design_notes: Temporal Causal Inference.Rmd builds cohort-by-membership-age summaries and plots treated vs control cohort activity. Causal Forests.R runs grf causal forests by cohort and an lm of forest effects on covariates. Local Linear Causal Forests Simulations.R: felm(log_act ~ ...) on simulated data.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. The README says the data cannot be shared under an NDA, that a 'sample of de-identified and simulated data' is provided, and that some code was redacted.
